messages:
Ava (Design): Quick run-through of the TileFlow idea — goal is a compact latency+throughput strip that sits above the heatmap so you can scan overall patterns without opening panels. thoughts?
Sam (Frontend): Like the idea. Concern: stacking sparkline ribbon + mini-map could be visually noisy at small widths.
Diego (Eng Runtime): From infra side: we can emit a summarized 'interval' trace per minute that's lower-cardinality. Should keep tokens cheap.
Priya (Product): Main use case is quick incident triage: see anomalous band and jump the scrubber to that interval. Need a clear affordance for "jump to anomaly".
Ava (Design): Agreed — proposal: a subtle chevron▶ that appears on hover on any tile to jump the scrubber. Arrow should be 24px tappable.
Marta (A11y): Accessibility nits: hover-only controls are a no-go for keyboard/screenreader users. Make it focusable and include aria-label="Jump to interval" and keyboard shortcut (e.g., press Enter).
Sam (Frontend): Implementation note: focus styles currently get stripped in mini tiles. We should keep a 2px outline with 3:1 contrast for dense density modes.
Ava (Design): Good call. Also thinking about a condensed legend: tiny icons for p50/p95/p99 with colorblind-safe palette. Feedback?
Priya (Product): Colorblind-safe is must. Also add a toggle to collapse percentiles into a single 'percentile mode' to reduce visual clutter for non-power users.
Diego (Eng Runtime): One engineering constraint: when percentile mode is collapsed we still need underlying sample distribution for debug — keep it behind long-press or alt-click so it doesn't slow the normal render path.
Sam (Frontend): Performance: render mini-map as an offscreen canvas and composite. That reduces DOM thrash on scrubbing. Will prototype.
Marta (A11y): Copy tweak: instead of "mini-map" use "interval navigator" in aria labels, so it sounds more functional. Also provide a visible focus ring and change tooltip timing to 300ms for discoverability.
Ava (Design): UX question: when user pins an interval to compare, should the tile strip freeze (show pinned state) or duplicate the tile into a comparison row?
Priya (Product): Duplicate into comparison row — makes multi-interval comparisons explicit. Add small badge like "1/3 pinned".
Diego (Eng Runtime): For pinned intervals we need to store KV of interval ids per user session; simple, but watch retention if customers pin many. Default cap at 5 pins.
Sam (Frontend): UI edgecase: when density mode is "ultra-compact" the tappable area collapses. Plan: switch to a longpress as the primary gesture on touch for compact mode.
Marta (A11y): Longpress is tough for keyboard users. Always expose a keyboard action in the overflow menu "Pin interval".
Ava (Design): Copy nits: tooltip copy for the chevron: "Jump to interval — opens inspector" vs "Jump to interval — focus timeline". Which is clearer?
Priya (Product): "Jump to interval — focus timeline" is better, inspector implies a separate modal.
Sam (Frontend): Small implementation detail: use data-interval-id attribute so analytics can capture usage without extra payload.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: design-proto/tileflow-mini-map v1 -> staging at 2024-06-22T15:30Z :rocket:
Ava (Design): Next steps: Sam to prototype canvas approach, Marta will write accessible interaction spec, Diego will stub interval summary endpoint, Priya will update product PRD. I'll follow up with a Figma clickthrough by EOD tomorrow. :+1:
Sam (Frontend): On it. Will push a prototype branch and drop link here when ready.
Marta (A11y): I'll add keyboard matrix and screenreader walkthrough to the doc.
Diego (Eng Runtime): I'll add a lightweight endpoint: /v1/tileflow/intervals?range=... that returns minute-level aggregates.
Priya (Product): Great — if this lands, ops can triage faster and customers get fewer false positives.
Ava (Design): Thanks all — super actionable. Will update the PRD with the decisions above and attach Figma before the next sync. :sparkles:
